Fig. 3. Individual particles were then identiﬁed by locating circular objects in the images. The average pixel intensity of the identiﬁed particles was calculated and used to assign species. It can be observed in Fig. 3, that the bright colored Delrin particles often had internal air pockets, which appeared as dark enclaves in their X-ray images and were often caught as particles dues to their cir- cular shape, giving rise to image recognition errors. These air pock- ets caused an artiﬁcial drop in the average pixel intensities of those particles thereby causing additional image recognition errors in species assignment. As the size of the particles was known, a size ﬁlter was used whereby only circular objects with diameters within 20 % of the average particle diameter were identiﬁed.
